correctness.rationale: The length-m orbit has total probability m^(-s)/zeta(s) and positive mass at every phase. Two forward marks recover the orbit and phase and occur for every point by length 2m, proving generation. A two-mark atom is a singleton of return time m; a single mark at i is one point per compatible orbit with minimum length max(i+1,n-i); two consecutive phases on an orbit of length at least n+2 witness overlap one for the zero word. The word with a mark at position zero only attains n, so the maximum is exactly n. Counting phases in these three cases also gives the exact moment identity. The lower sum over m<=floor(n/2) and the upper bound from min(m,n) give the stated powers and critical logarithmic coefficients; pointwise monotone convergence gives the finite limits. Subtracting the squared mean does not cancel the leading divergent second moment. Singleton entropy is finite by summability of m^(-s) log m, the increasing forward-join entropies tend to it, and the generating entropy rate is zero. This yields infinite system-level mean for 1<s<=2 and infinite system-level variance through s=3; the finite mean asserted for the intermediate regime concerns this partition. The packaged checker.py and VERIFICATION.md were read, not run; their rational finite-truncation checks are supplementary to the infinite argument.
